name: Denmark

items.label: ATP pension contribution
items.note: DKK 99.00 a month for full-time employees: a third of the DKK 891 a quarter (the employer pays the other two thirds).

items.label: Pension contribution
items.note: Your share of an employer-administered (labour market) pension, as a percentage of pay. It cannot exceed pay left after ATP and AM-bidrag.

items.label: Pension contribution after AM-bidrag
items.note: AM-bidrag is still paid on the contribution (it stays in the AM-bidrag base, AMBL §2 stk. 1 nr. 4); the rest comes off personal income before tax.

items.label: Employment deduction (beskæftigelsesfradrag)
items.note: 12.75% of pay, at most DKK 63,300. Pension contributions to employer schemes count towards it (LL §9 J refers to the AM-bidrag base).

items.label: Job deduction (jobfradrag)
items.note: 4.5% of income above DKK 235,200, at most DKK 3,100.

items.label: Municipal tax (kommuneskat)
items.note: The national average rate, on taxable income above the DKK 54,100 personal allowance. Rates range from about 23.4% to 26.3%.

items.label: Church tax (kirkeskat)
items.note: Members of the Church of Denmark only; about 0.87% on average.

items.label: State tax (bundskat, mellemskat, topskat)
items.note: Bottom tax 12.01% above the allowance; middle tax 7.5% above DKK 641,200; top tax 7.5% above DKK 777,900; top-top tax 5% above DKK 2,592,700 (the new 2026 structure).

items.label: Pension contribution
items.note: What reaches your pension: the contribution less the 8% AM-bidrag on it.

assumptions: No pension contributions through pay; each person is taxed individually
notModelled: Interest, union dues, commuting and other deductions
Private (non-employer) pension savings and the employer's share of contributions

obtainedFrom.note: Employer-scheme pension contributions are deducted before A-skat, are in the AM-bidrag basis (AMBL §2 stk. 1 nr. 4) and therefore in the employment deduction basis (LL §9 J).
